Lore
LOR
noun (Gen-Z slang)
From Old English lār, teaching, learning (kin to learn). Fantasy fiction and video games (the Elder Scrolls and Dark Souls series are the usual examples) used lore for the backstory of an invented world, often hidden in item descriptions for players to piece together. In the early 2020s TikTok turned the word on people: a person’s lore is his backstory, and a lore drop is a revealing story from his past ("the lore runs deep").

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang lore is backstory — the hidden history of a game world, or, more and more, of a person: "wait, what’s the lore?" means "how did this happen?" and a lore drop is an old story that suddenly explains someone. The Christian observation: this is one of the most redeemable words in the language, because Christianity has the deepest lore of all, and God commands that it be told. Israel was to answer the child’s question: "when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies" (Deu 6:20). The psalmist made it a family duty: "We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD" (Psa 78:4), and the next generation sang it back: "our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days" (Psa 44:1). When the lore is not passed down, the result is the book of Judges: "there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD" (Jdg 2:10). Paul adds the one warning: not every backstory edifies; give no heed to "fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions" (1Ti 1:4). A father tells his son: you know the lore of your favourite game down to the last item description; learn the lore of your own family and your own church, the true story of what God has done, and be ready to tell it to your children.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (fantasy and video-game backstory; applied to people on TikTok, early 2020s) for the hidden history behind a world or a person — and the faith has the deepest lore of all, which fathers are commanded to tell (Psa 78:4).

LORE, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2020–present; gaming and fandom origin) The backstory of a game, a series, or a person. "Okay but what’s the lore behind you and your cousin not talking?"

Lore drop, a revealing story from someone’s past. Deep lore, obscure backstory only devoted fans know. "The lore thickens."

Older sense, still current: learning or teaching handed down, as folklore, sea lore, the lore of the elders.

Webster (1828), root word lore: “LORE, noun Learning; doctrine; lesson; instruction. The law of nations, or the lore of war. Lo! Rome herself, proud mistress now no more of arts, but thundering against heathen lore”

Decode for parents: your teen is asking for the story behind things. Tell them God’s, and your family’s.

Key Scripture

Deu 6:20 — "And when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments, which the LORD our God hath commanded you?"

Psa 78:4 — "We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done."

Psa 44:1 — "To the chief Musician for the sons of Korah, Maschil. We have heard with our ears, O God, our fathers have told us, what work thou didst in their days, in the times of old."

Jdg 2:10 — "And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel."

1Ti 1:4 — "Neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith: so do."

Modern Corruption

Lore is an honest word for backstory with little corruption of its own; the drift is a generation that knows a game’s lore by heart and the lore of the LORD not at all.

expand to see more

There is nothing wrong with enjoying a well-built story world. The trouble is proportion. A boy can explain the hidden history of a video game across three sequels and cannot tell you who Gideon was or why his grandfather joined the church he did. That is not an accident; whoever tells the stories forms the child. The book of Judges shows what a nation looks like one generation after the lore stopped being told: "there arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel" (Jdg 2:10).

God’s answer is the family table. The Passover was built around a child’s question (Deu 6:20); the stones at the Jordan were set up so that children would ask what they meant (Jos 4:6). Paul’s warning keeps it honest: not all backstory edifies, and "endless genealogies" and speculation can crowd out faith (1Ti 1:4). Tell the true lore — creation, fall, redemption, and the works of God in your own family — and tell it until your children can tell it back to theirs (Psa 78:4).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English lār (teaching) → lore, knowledge handed down → fantasy and game backstory → early-2020s TikTok: a person’s lore, a lore drop.

2000s–2010s video games: backstory hidden in item text and ruins

Usage

"Tell your children the lore of the LORD (Psa 78:4)."

"One generation without the lore, and you get Judges 2:10."
